newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical unit workers sue over benefits.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical unit workers sue over benefits.

text.p: Thirty-eight current and former employees of Dow Environmental Inc, a unit of Dow Chemical Co, have sued Dow Environmental and Dow Chemical for alleged unlawful termination of retirement benefits in the form of stock appreciation rights, the plaintiffs said Monday.
The group said that under a plan created in 1991, certain Dow Environmental executives, senior managers and administrative personnel were awarded the stock rights as deferred compensation.

While Dow Environmental's profits grew "dramatically" between 1991 and 1994 and despite Dow Chemical's projection that Dow Environmental would continue to grow, the two companies terminated the stock appreciation rights in 1995, they said.
The group said the stock rights were projected to be worth $1,000 to $2,000 a share, but "the employees were paid nothing." The terminated retirement benefits involves $20 million, they said.

The lawsuit alleges further that the cancellation of the stock rights violated the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, which imposes restrictions on employers' ability to cancel benefits which provide retirement income.

"An employer should not be able to promise a retirement benefit or other deferred compensation or benefit and then renege on that promise after the fact," said David Barmak, a Washington D.C. lawyer representing the plaintiffs.
The two companies were not immediately available to comment.
